notes: Class 10 English literature, generated by tooling/scripts/build_fresh_papers.py. Section A is compulsory (two questions), Section B offers three and asks for any two. The student answers both of A, then 5 and 3 of B in that order, so B/4 is not required rather than unanswered -- the distinction this paper exists to test. Five marks each; twenty available over the four that count, and B/4 leaves the denominator as well as the numerator. Every authored answer is a strong one, which makes this the paper that detects OVER-penalisation: if the marker is systematically harsh, this is where it shows, because there is nothing here to legitimately deduct for. Bands are one mark wide throughout, since five-mark literature responses are the least determinate marking on any of these papers.

questions.key: How weather figures the speaker's state of mind, with textual support and a sense of development across the poem rather than a single observation.
questions.note: Tracks three stages -- drizzle, remembered sun, breaking storm -- maps each to the speaker's state, and quotes. Development plus quotation plus an interpretation of the ending is the full tariff.

questions.key: The brothers' relationship AS IT CHANGES: closeness, the rupture after the father's death, and the qualified reconciliation. Marks require the trajectory, not a static description.
questions.note: Gives all three stages, quotes the estrangement, and the closing qualification -- 'quieter than before, not the same' -- is the point that shows the change was not simply undone.

questions.key: The writer's attitude to the village, WITH a phrase quoted in support, as the question explicitly requires. A balanced reading beats a one-sided one.
questions.note: Holds affection and criticism together, quotes as instructed, and the final clause states the balance outright. Answered second of the two in Section B and on a later page than 5, which is the out-of-order case.

questions.excluded_reason: The paper offers any two of three in Section B and the student answered two. This question was legitimately skipped, so there is no mark to be right about -- a zero here would be as wrong as a mark. Carried in truth so that a run reporting it as unanswered, or marking it, is visible as a fault.

questions.key: A judgement on the ending -- hopeful or bleak -- with reasons drawn from the text. A position is required; a summary is not an answer.
questions.note: Takes a position, qualifies it ('hopeful but only just'), concedes the bleak evidence, and rests the judgement on a specific choice the narrator makes. Answered first of the two in Section B, before 3.
